title: Semantic Router: On the Feasibility of Hijacking MLLMs via a Single Adversarial Perturbation
claim: A single universal perturbation can act as a semantic router, steering sequential stateless decisions to attacker-chosen outputs based on input content.
layout: 2 regions: left attacker panel, right timeline of 3 frames; left-to-right
description: The figure shows a threat model for hijacking a multimodal LLM that drives a vehicle. A rounded panel on the left holds a map with a red start pin, a blue destination arrow and a red-and-blue route. Below the map, an attacker icon says 'Drive as I told you.' A blank 'Noise Frame' is pasted onto the MLLM eye icon. On the right, a timeline arrow labeled 'Decision Sequence' runs from a car at Start through timestamps 03:56, 09:03 and 15:46. Under each timestamp is a real street-view frame with a faint noise border. Beneath the frames are red headings 'Hijacked Decision 1/2/3' and orange speech boxes with targets: 'Turn right at this intersection', 'Turn left within the roundabout', 'Stop near the Euro flag'. The eye goes first to the map, then along the timeline.
caption: Illustration of the threat model of semantic-aware hijacking. As the MLLM processes the image sequences, the perturbation acts as a semantic router, forcing the model to output the attacker's predefined targets based on the input semantics, cumulatively guiding the vehicle to a predefined destination.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in stateless systems, such as autonomous driving and robotics. This paper investigates a novel threat: Semantic-Aware Hijacking. We explore the feasibility of hijacking multiple stateless decisions simultaneously using a single universal perturbation. We introduce the Semantic-Aware Universal Perturbation (SAUP), which acts as a semantic router, "actively" perceiving input semantics and routing them to distinct, attacker-defined targets. To achieve this, we conduct theoretical and empirical analysis on the geometric properties in the latent space. Guided by these insights, we propose the Semantic-Oriented (SORT) optimization strategy and annotate a new dataset with fine-grained semantics to evaluate performance. Extensive experiments on three representative MLLMs demonstrate the fundamental feasibility of this attack, achieving a 66% attack success rate over five targets using a single frame against Qwen.
